ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, senior managers, and authorized signatories against: (i) United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List; (iii) New Zealand Sanctions Act 2019 sanctions list; (iv) Swiss/European Union sanctions frameworks where applicable; (v) New Zealand PEP register notified by the FIU; (vi) all domestic police and FIU adverse media alerts. Screening is required prior to incorporation and periodically thereafter, with a written compliance file retained for at least five years per AML/CFT Act 2009 Part 1.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – online registration system (accessible via https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in English (using ASCII alphabet); if a Māori or other non-English script is used, an official English transliteration is required and must accompany the registration. The name must not be misleading or confusing in the context of New Zealand law and commerce. Company names may use numbers and Latin script only after careful review for similarity to existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar refuses a name reservation, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration within 15 working days of the refusal, stating substantive arguments and any secondary proposed names, per the Companies Act 1993 sections 20–22. If reconsideration is refused, the applicant may appeal the decision to the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016. An existing name reservation may be extended once for a further 20 working days before expiry by filing the prescribed extension request and fee; after expiry, a new application must be lodged.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only insofar as the virtual office provider maintains a physical street address in New Zealand, is staffed to accept legal process, and does not operate purely as a mail-forwarding service. For a bulk port stevedoring terminal, the registered office must align with the geographic location of the principal place of business or an explicit registered address in the jurisdiction where the operator receives official notifications. Purely virtual offices without physical premises for the acceptance of legal documents are not permissible for this licensed activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. Regulators including Maritime New Zealand, the NZ Port Authorities, and the Occupational Safety and Health division of WorkSafe New Zealand routinely conduct unannounced physical inspections. Likelihood is quantified at 70% probability of an on-site inspection within the first 12 months of operation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 12 (incorporation), 13 (application for registration), 20 (certificate of incorporation), 22 (name reservation), 106 (registered office), 122-126 (directors), 189 (statutory records), and 203 (amalgamations); also the Overseas Investment Act 2005 for non-resident investment screening.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (electronic incorporation application via the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Companies Act 1993; shares may be allotted at par, at a premium, or for no consideration as authorised by the constitution; no escrow account requirement is imposed by the Companies Act 1993. Non-resident ownership of the port terminal is permitted, but if the terminal involves sensitive land or significant business assets, the Overseas Investment Act 2005 consent may be required with the foreign investor lodging documentary evidence of funds rather than a paid-in capital escrow.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [CK IC / NEW ZEALAND OPERATING COMPANY], ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE COMPANIES ACT 1993 AND THE CONSTITUTION OF THE COMPANY.

WHEREAS the company is incorporated as a limited liability company under the laws of New Zealand, and
WHEREAS the board wishes to effect the initial corporate organisation of the company.

NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: That the allotment of the initial share capital be and is hereby authorised, approved and confirmed; that the subscribers to the incorporation application be allotted the number of ordinary shares set out in the share register on the terms disclosed in the application for registration; that the shares be issued upon payment of the agreed consideration, if any, in compliance with the Companies Act 1993; and that the directors be and are hereby authorised to open the share register, issue share certificates, and call for payment of any unpaid capital as required by the board.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: That the physical office situated at the address first recorded with the Registrar of Companies and shown in the incorporation application is hereby adopted as the registered office of the company; and that the directors are authorised to notify the Registrar of the registered office address, to maintain the statutory registers at that address, and to effect any change of address as the board considers necessary.

3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: That the following officers be and are hereby appointed to hold office until the next annual meeting of shareholders, subject to the Companies Act 1993 and the constitution: (a) [Name], director; (b) [Name], director; (c) [Name], company secretary, where applicable; (d) [Name], chief financial officer; and (e) [Name], authorised banking signatory. The authorised signatories shall act singly or jointly as designated in the banking mandate and shall have power to execute banking, port authority, stevedoring licence, and governmental documents, and to procure the opening of bank accounts and the giving of security on behalf of the company.

4. BANK ACCOUNTS AND CORPORATE SEAL: That the banking authorities and corporate seal, if adopted, be approved; that the directors be authorised to open bank accounts with the approved financial institutions; and that the officers be instructed to file all statutory returns with the Companies Office and Inland Revenue.

5. TAX AND INDUSTRIAL FILINGS: That management be authorised to apply to the Inland Revenue Department for tax, GST, and employer registrations and to file all applications for the port facility security approval, stevedoring operating licence, resource consents, and environmental permits described in the formation dossier.

ADOPTED at [Auckland], New Zealand, on this [date], such resolutions being effective immediately without a meeting, pursuant to section 91 of the Companies Act 1993 and the constitution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and NZBN availability check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) - NZBN online register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a search on the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register to confirm that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or a name reserved by another person. Where protection of a specific trading name is desired, file an application to reserve the name under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993. For a foreign-owned bulk stevedoring terminal, also undertake a preliminary Overseas Investment Act 2005 sensitive-activity screening to ensure the name and business purpose will not be exposed to later objection. The application is lodged electronically through the Companies Office portal with the proposed name, the applicant's details, and the intended incorporation date.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name
NZBN name search confirmation sheet
Name reservation application under section 22, Companies Act 1993
Preliminary overseas investment assessment
Identity documents of the reserving person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is identical or too similar to an existing name, the Registrar will query the application; the applicant may file a statutory declaration of consent of the prior name holder, submit an alternative name, or apply for review of the Registrar's decision with an appeal to the High Court under Part 9 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of constitution, director consents, and statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) - pre-filing review
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution, or adopt the statutory default in Schedule 2 of the Companies Act 1993, setting out share classes, restrictions on share transfers, director powers, remuneration, and the procedures for board and shareholder meetings. Obtain signed consents to act as directors from at least one director resident in New Zealand or, in the case of a foreign-controlled operating company, a locally appointed director and local agent. Complete the initial allotment schedule, the share register, and the register of shareholders, and record the proposed registered office, which must be a physical address in New Zealand, together with a service address. All documents are prepared in English and retained for the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Constitution of the company (if not adopting the statutory default)
Consent to act as director for each director
Share register and initial allotment schedule
Registered office and address for service particulars
Identification documents for each director and shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries defective consents or constitution clauses, the company may file an amended constitution or cure the consent deficiency online; a refusal may be appealed to the High Court under Part 9 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of incorporation application and payment of statutory fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration of a Company through the Companies Office online portal (NZBN). Enter the company type (limited liability company), registered office address, full legal names and residential addresses of directors and shareholders, details of the initial share allotment, and the adopted constitution. Authorise the filing digitally and pay the statutory registration fee, currently NZD 100 for online filing. Upon successful processing, the Registrar issues a certificate of incorporation and a New Zealand Business Number; the board then adopts the resolutions contained in the pro forma first board resolution. Ensure that any Court- or Registrar-imposed condition on the use of the name is satisfied before the certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Incorporation application (Companies Office electronic form)
Adopted constitution
Certified copies of passports and proof of residential address for directors
Banker's confirmation of share subscription funds, if any
Payment of NZD 100 statutory registration fee
Consent to act as director forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application does not satisfy the Companies Act 1993, the Registrar will give notice of rejection within the statutory period; the applicant may file a new application, submit a solicitor's letter addressing the defect, or apply to the High Court for an order directing registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of registered office and statutory register compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and local authority where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure that the registered office is a physical location in New Zealand, commonly the office of the company's principal agent or counsel. Maintain all statutory records at that office, including the share register, director and shareholder registers, minute books, and accounting records, in accordance with section 189 of the Companies Act 1993. Notify the Registrar in writing of any change of registered office within 10 working days. For the bulk stevedoring terminal, establish a corporate governance handbook, an authorised signatory matrix for banking and port authority clearing, a delegations register for the port operations manager, and a corporate risk register covering safety, environmental, and maritime liabilities.
required_dossiers: Registered office address confirmation and evidence of right to occupy
Company records book containing statutory registers
Consent for physical inspection of records
Corporate governance manual
Delegated authorities matrix and risk register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to maintain a registered office or records is an offence under the Act; the company may immediately file a change of address notice online, or a director may apply to the Registrar or the court for an order to rectify the records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and employer registration with Inland Revenue and Accident Compensation Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand, and Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the certificate of incorporation, apply for the company's tax file number through the Inland Revenue online business registration service or by filing form IR450. Register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if the taxable supply of stevedoring and terminal services is expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period. Register as an employer for PAYE, KiwiSaver, and fringe benefit tax, and obtain an ACC employer levy account for the stevedoring workforce. Notify the port company finance office of the new operating entity to allow activation of the Port Authority Clearing payment rail and SWIFT wire instructions, and register the terminal as a customs-controlled area with the New Zealand Customs Service where hold or inspection of cargo occurs.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN
IRD business registration form (IR450)
Forecast turnover statement for GST registration
Employment agreements and payroll details for stevedoring staff
ACC employer registration particulars
Port authority clearing account instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue queries the registration, the company may submit an amended business registration or an objection through the myIR portal; administrative determinations are subject to review under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Port, environmental, and physical licensing applications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regional Council (Resource Management Act 1991), Maritime New Zealand, and the port company / harbourmaster
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply in parallel for (a) a berth access or site lease agreement with the port company; (b) land-use and discharge consents from the Regional Council, including a full Assessment of Environmental Effects where the terminal constitutes a new or expanded activity; (c) port facility security approval from Maritime New Zealand under the Maritime Security Act 2004 and ISPS Code; (d) a hazardous substances location approval from WorkSafe / FENZ where cranes, fuels, and lubricants are stored; and (e) building consent and a code compliance certificate for fixed terminal infrastructure under the Building Act 2004. The applicant must submit a stevedoring operations manual, cargo-handling plans for bulk commodities, a vessel traffic communication protocol, a marine oil-spill response plan, and a civil defence emergency plan. Upon issuance of the operating licence and consents, the company may begin terminal operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN
Resource consent application with Assessment of Environmental Effects
Terminal operations and stevedoring procedures manual
Berth occupancy and vessel scheduling plan
Port facility security and ISPS plan
Building consent and structural engineering certificates
Fire safety and hazardous substances location certificates
Oil spill and emergency response plans
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the consent authority identifies deficiencies in the application, the applicant may file a supplementary statement, request a pre-hearing meeting, or appeal the decision to the Environment Court under the Resource Management Act 1991; refusals of building consent may be appealed to the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Harbourmaster's office of the relevant port company, acting with Maritime New Zealand and the Regional Council as the resource-consent authority; employment and occupational safety supervision is exercised by WorkSafe New Zealand within the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Stevedoring Operating Licence / Port Facility Security Approval under the Maritime Security Act 2004, issued by Maritime New Zealand, together with a berth-access or terminal operating agreement with the port company.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (New Zealand) and the relevant Regional Council under the Resource Management Act 1991, with the Board of Inquiry for nationally significant projects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE) for a new bulk stevedoring terminal, unless the activity is already a permitted activity within an operative port designation or regional plan; in that case a controlled or limited-notified resource consent may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Air Quality) 2004 for particulate matter, nitrogen oxides, volatile organic compounds, and diesel emissions; wastewater and ballast water discharge limits under the regional coastal plan and the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Sources of Human Drinking Water) 2007; hazardous substances handling under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996; oil waste and oily water must be discharged to port reception facilities in accordance with MARPOL Annex I; noise limits under the district plan; and compliance with the Exclusive Economic Zone and Continental Shelf (Environmental Effects) Act 2012 where offshore transshipment occurs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; structural load and building compliance certificates under the Building Act 2004; emergency and evacuation planning under the Civil Defence Emergency Management Act 2002; occupational health and safety clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including a hazardous-substances location certificate under the Health and Safety at Work (Hazardous Substances) Regulations 2017; and a maritime safety and safe-ship-management clearance from Maritime New Zealand for stevedoring craft and terminal interfaces.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand – central portal 'myIR' administered at www.ird.govt.nz; the New Zealand Customs Service (NZCS) manages border and export declaration systems with integrated reporting to the IRD for GST purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand must first obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) via the New Zealand Companies Office and then apply to the IRD for an IRD number (8-9 digit unique tax identifier). For GST purposes, the entity files Form GST 1 (Registration of Person for GST) or the non-resident variant GST 2, providing the registered office address, principal place of business, expected turnover, and evidence of foreign incorporation. The IRD issues the IRD number and GST registration certificate within 5-10 business days; registration is retroactive to the date the taxable activity commenced or the date the entity first exceeded the NZD 60,000 threshold. If the entity is a non-resident company not incorporated in New Zealand, it must also appoint a local agent for service of process (under section 336 of the Companies Act 1993) and disclose the ultimate holding company structure for BEPS and controlled foreign company (CFC) reporting purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope with entity-level taxation for resident companies; the subject 'International Company' (CK_IC) is classified internally as Tax_Exempt_Zone only in respect of foreign-sourced income of a non-resident company. Under the Income Tax Act 2007, a non-resident company is taxable only on income that has a source in New Zealand; income derived wholly overseas is exempt. However, stevedoring services physically performed at New Zealand marine docks (bulk cargo loading/unloading) have a New Zealand source (the services are performed in New Zealand and are directly connected with land and goods situated in New Zealand at the time of supply), hence that income is within the New Zealand tax net. The entity is therefore a New Zealand taxable branch of a non-resident company, subject to New Zealand corporate income tax at the standard rate of 28% on its New Zealand-source business profits, and to GST on its taxable supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' classification regime. Elections available include: (i) under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018, the Commissioner of Inland Revenue may adjust treatment of hybrid or reverse-hybrid entities; (ii) a non-resident company may elect to apply the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) regime (2% levy on interest paid to non-residents) instead of non-resident withholding tax; (iii) a non-resident company can elect for a branch equivalent tax account (BETA) or for the use of the branch equivalent method; (iv) for GST, division 60 of the GST Act 1985 permits a non-resident to elect to appoint a New Zealand-resident agent for GST compliance; and (v) hybrid mismatch elections under the Tax Administration Act 1994 must be disclosed using IRD form IR858 to neutralise deduction/no-inclusion outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) – a comprehensive value-added tax on consumption supplied in New Zealand, imposed under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (GSTA).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period (for both resident and non-resident persons); once exceeded, mandatory registration is required within 21 days. For non-residents supplying 'remote services' (electronically supplied services, telecommunications, digital services) to New Zealand-based consumers, an additional registration threshold of NZD 60,000 of remote-service supplies applies. Because the stevedoring terminal supplies services physically performed in New Zealand, the standard threshold applies, and the entity must register and charge GST at 15% on all supplies, unless zero-rating applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand operates a voluntary electronic invoicing regime (no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance). E-invoicing follows the Peppol framework and is available via certified service providers; no digital stamping or pre-clearance tax authority approval is required. GST returns must be filed electronically through myIR (mandatory for GST-registered persons with annual turnover exceeding NZD 30,000) on a monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly basis. The IRD performs automated data matching with bank transactions and NZCS border data. A 'buyer-created tax invoice' mechanism exists under section 24D of the GSTA for port terminal operators, subject to prior IRD approval, and all invoices must contain the tax invoice statement 'Includes GST'. Digital asset record keeping is acceptable, and e-invoicing via Peppol is presumed compliant.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under section 11 of the GSTA applies to: (a) goods physically exported from New Zealand within 28 days of supply, evidenced by customs documentation; (b) services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply and who does not use the services in New Zealand, except where the services are supplied in connection with land in New Zealand, or with goods in New Zealand at the time of supply; (c) international transport, insurance, and vessel-refueling services. For the bulk port stevedoring terminal, the core stevedoring service (vessel loading/unloading at a marine dock) is performed in New Zealand and is directly in connection with New Zealand land and with cargo physically present in New Zealand; consequently it does not qualify for zero-rating as a service to a non-resident and must be taxed at 15%, regardless of the invoicing currency. Only ancillary services provided to a non-resident outside New Zealand (e.g., offshore freight forwarding, dispatch documentation services, or fees for services supplied remotely to the ship owner while the vessel is outside New Zealand waters) can be zero-rated. The entity may claim input tax credits on all GST-bearing costs, and any excess credits are refundable by the IRD within 21 days of the return being filed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Electronic Cargo Movement Reference / CUSR) as filed with the New Zealand Customs Service and the Integrated Cargo System (ICS) export clearance confirmation
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill evidencing the export of the cargo from a New Zealand port, with the vessel name, voyage number, port of loading, and port of discharge

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or Foreign Exchange Contract confirmation from a registered New Zealand bank or NZX-regulated foreign exchange dealer evidencing receipt of the foreign currency settlement within the prescribed repatriation window

Port Terminal Service Order and Vessel Operations Report (including stevedoring time sheets and tally clerk records) demonstrating that the supply was physically performed and linked to the export cargo, and the final GST return and tax invoice set if the supply is claimed as zero-rated
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to intensive IRD audit, including cross-referencing of NZCS export declarations, port operator records, shipping lines' manifests, and bank inflows. If the IRD determines that a supply was incorrectly zero-rated (e.g., services connected with New Zealand land or goods, or evidence of export is insufficient), the taxpayer is liable for the GST shortfall plus use-of-money interest from the original taxable period. Under the Tax Administration Act 1994, an unacceptable tax position attracts a shortfall penalty of 20% of the tax shortfall; gross carelessness increases the penalty to 40%, and intentional disregard or abuse of the zero-rating rules attracts a 150% penalty. Additionally, promoting or facilitating fraudulent zero-rating schemes carries a criminal penalty of up to NZD 50,000 for a first offence and up to NZD 100,000 for subsequent offences, and imprisonment for up to 10 years for knowingly providing false export documentation under the Crimes Act 1961. Where the wrongful zero-rating involves cross-border reimbursement or a related-party supply, the IRD may apply the general anti-avoidance provision (section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007) to reconstruct the transaction and disallow all associated input credits, with retrospective adjustment across up to four years (and longer in cases of fraud or absolute evasion).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) acting as prudential supervisor and administrator of the Exchange Settlement Account System; Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for wholesale market conduct; Overseas Investment Office (Toitū Te Whenua) for inward foreign direct investment screening under the Overseas Investment Act 2005.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is fully convertible under a free-floating exchange rate regime. There are no exchange controls on current account transactions (goods, services, dividends, interest, royalties) or capital account movements. Non-resident investors may freely repatriate dividends, branch profits, loan repayments, and disposed proceeds, subject only to reporting and AML/CFT documentation. Capital inflows for port terminal stevedoring operations are not subject to central bank approval; however, investments in 'sensitive' land or significant business assets may require Overseas Investment Office consent. The International Company (Tax-Exempt Zone) will be treated as a non-resident for CRS/FATCA classification, and all capital account remittances must be supported by legal ownership and source-of-funds documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters of stevedoring and cargo-handling services may retain USD and other foreign currency receipts in resident foreign currency accounts or offshore accounts at their discretion. Cross-border transactions above NZD 10,000 equivalent must be reported to the transacting bank for Reserve Bank Balance of Payments statistics, and banks are required to comply with screening under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act). Invoicing of port services in USD with settlement to the NZ operational account is lawful; conversion to NZD is a commercial decision of the IC.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (NZD) with Foreign Currency Account (USD, AUD)
Operational Account (NZD) + FX Forward Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account (for inbound equity injection) + Operational Account
Operational Account (NZD) + Receivables Account for Export Proceeds

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low as a primary operating bank; Medium only as a supplemental payment corridor. New Zealand does not maintain an electronic money institution (EMI) licensing regime; offshore digital EMIs cannot provide NZD deposit liabilities, credit, or direct access to the domestic BECS/SWIFT clearing system. An offshore EMI may operate only under Financial Service Provider (FSP) registration and a bespoke AML/CFT compliance programme, with settlement held through a NZ incorporated bank. Such arrangements do not satisfy the commercial substance and domestic payment requirements of port concession agreements, nor do they provide committed FX lines or documentary trade services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted under New Zealand banking practice; there is no statutory physical appearance mandate for directors of non-resident companies. The bank may accept electronic identity verification with biometric liveness checks, certified passport copies, and a live video interview conducted by the AML/CFT compliance officer. For a Cook Islands International Company (offshore tax-exempt zone), the bank will typically require: (i) board resolution certified by the registered agent; (ii) apostilled or notarized Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, and Register of Directors/Shareholders issued within 90 days; (iii) individual video interviews of all authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owners; and (iv) possible in-person verification at an NZ branch or designated overseas correspondent where the UBO risk rating is High.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-exempt International Company (Cook Islands) with opaque beneficial ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO chain certification issued by the licensed registered agent; trust deed or declaration of trust identifying settlor, protector, and beneficiaries; Cook Islands Financial Service Provider licence confirmation; NZ counsel legal opinion confirming the entity operates a genuine stevedoring terminal concession and is not a shell.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of initial capital injection from non-resident trust corpus or foreign discretionary trust
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for the IC covering the most recent 3 years where available; sworn source-of-wealth report prepared by a licensed reporting entity; bank references from the funding institution; evidence of commercial substance including the port authority concession agreement, equipment leases, and projected cargo handling volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction flags associated with offshore registry and corporate-tax-exempt status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FATF mutual evaluation excerpt confirming Cook Islands is not grey-listed; CRS registration certificate from Cook Islands Ministry of Finance and NZ IRD; tax residency certificate; Enhanced Due Diligence questionnaire addressing political exposure, sanctions screening, and regulatory status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or adverse media screening match against corporate name or UBO
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: International sanctions database search result with nil-match or waiver/resolution letter; name-change deed where applicable; independent counsel opinion; committed transaction monitoring protocol with the bank's financial crime unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Stated account purpose and projected transaction flows inconsistent with bulk port stevedoring scope
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed port terminal concession or port access agreement with the Port Authority; statutory stevedoring authorisation under the Maritime Transport Act 1994 and port bylaws; pro-forma invoices and vessel call schedules; 12-month cash flow projection segregating opex, capex, and FX hedging flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing from the Cook Islands International Company to the NZ operational bank: remit via SWIFT MT103 using OECD BOP purpose code '1.1 Investment in equity capital'; provide the receiving bank with the NZ Companies Office shareholder resolution, share allotment statement, and confirmation that Overseas Investment Act 2005 consent is not required for non-sensitive port services; route initial funds to the Capital Escrow Account and subsequently to the Operational Account after Enhanced Due Diligence completion; submit IRD CRS self-certification and FATCA classification; retain source-of-funds records for at least five years. No RBNZ exchange control approval is required, but remittances exceeding NZD 100,000 may trigger balance of payments statistical reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border supplier payments (stevedoring equipment, crane spares, international payroll) using OECD purpose codes; (ii) domestic BECS (Bulk Electronic Clearing System) and direct entry credits for port dues, wharfage, environmental levies, and payroll clearing to NZ entities; (iii) commercial Letters of Credit issued by NZ banks under UCP 600 for capital equipment imports, settled by MT103/MT202 against shipping documents; (iv) resident foreign currency accounts and executed FX forwards for settlement of USD-denominated port authority invoices and vessel agency charges; (v) SWIFT gpi tracking for end-to-end transparency. All outbound remittances above NZD 10,000 equivalent are screened for AML/CTF, sanctions, and BOP reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (NZD/USD, NZD/AUD, NZD/EUR) with maturities up to 12 months
Outright Spot and forward contracts for port revenue conversion
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for restricted Asian currencies (CNH, IDR, VND, PHP, INR) as required for sub-contractor payments
Cross-Currency Swaps (NZD/USD floating-to-floating and fixed-to-floating) for long-term port terminal financing
Vanilla FX Options (puts and calls) for hedge-only purposes with no leverage
FX Swaps for working capital management between USD receipts and NZD operational disbursements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the Cook Islands International Company (registered office, registered agent, directors and shareholders details) and Annual Renewal of Certificate of Compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) – Registrar of International Companies, Cook Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on each anniversary of incorporation; the licensed Cook Islands registered agent must file the return and pay the renewal fee by the anniversary date, with FSC tolerance for late renewal generally limited to 30 days and always subject to penalty
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty accrues from the first month after the anniversary; continued default is reportable by the registered agent to the FSC and, ordinarily within 3 to 6 months of default, triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution of the company; restoration is possible only on court order with payment of all arrears, penalties and costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Renewal Levy (authorized-capital parity fee) paid with the Annual Return for continuation of the Certificate of Compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) / Cook Islands Government Treasury
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable on the incorporation anniversary each year simultaneously with the Annual Return; no statutory extension, any grace period being purely discretionary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge imposed from the first day after the anniversary; default beyond the FSC strike-off notice period results in deregistration and dissolution of the company, with restoration only upon full settlement of overdue fees, penalties and legal costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Overseas-Company Annual Return to the New Zealand Companies Office (applicable only where the International Company itself carries on the bulk stevedoring/terminal business in New Zealand rather than holding a local operating subsidiary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month following the anniversary of the date of NZ overseas-company registration (Companies Act 1993, Part 14); filing available online
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of NZD 200; persistent non-filing leads to removal from the overseas companies register, and contracts made while the company is an unregistered overseas company are unenforceable by it in New Zealand courts

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit for the tax-exempt non-resident Cook Islands International Company unless it holds a financial-services licence (banking, insurance, trust company or other FSC-regulated activity) or audited accounts are required by its members, a secured creditor, parent company or court order. A New Zealand operating subsidiary in the stevedoring/port-terminal business is statutorily audited only if it satisfies the NZ 'large company' test under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 (total assets above NZD 60 million, total revenue above NZD 30 million, or 50 or more full-time employees).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); the Cook Islands International Companies Act permits accounts to be kept in any currency and under generally accepted accounting principles appropriate to the company's circumstances, with NZ operating subsidiaries applying NZ IFRS (IFRS-equivalent) for statutory reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Cook Islands maintains no public UBO register. On every share transfer, the board of the International Company approves the transfer and the registered agent updates the Register of Members at the registered office. Annually, the licensed registered agent performs a beneficial-ownership and AML/CFT file refresh, obtains confirmation from the company secretary of its current directors, members and ultimate beneficial owners, and records the confirmation in the agent's compliance file; disclosure to the FSC occurs only through the confidential Annual Return or a lawful information request, not by public filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 2,500 per annum, covering the licensed Cook Islands registered agent, registered office, company secretary and annual AML/CFT maintenance; representative-market range, varying with agent and volume
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required for the International Company; voluntary board/creditor-requested IC audit typically USD 8,000 – USD 15,000 per engagement, while a full statutory audit of a New Zealand bulk stevedoring operating subsidiary typically ranges USD 15,000 – USD 40,000 per annum

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand imposes no statutory tax holiday or free-zone exemption applicable to bulk-port stevedoring businesses; a taxpayer utilising the CK_IC International Company template will nonetheless be assessed at the 28% headline rate on all income sourced from terminal operations at a New Zealand port. Preferential deductions and credits available to a qualifying terminal operator include: (i) the R&D Tax Incentive, a 15% tax credit on eligible R&D expenditure (e.g., automated cargo-handling and safety systems) exceeding the NZD 50,000 annual minimum, with refundability available in certain loss-making scenarios; (ii) immediate expensing of low-value assets costing NZD 1,000 or less per item, and a reduced-cost threshold of NZD 5,000 per asset for taxpayers with annual turnover below NZD 5 million; (iii) ordinary depreciation deductions on wharves, bulk cranes, conveyor systems, and stevedoring equipment at the rates published in Inland Revenue's depreciation rate tables, including accelerated 'commissioning depreciation' for major port infrastructure; and (iv) the available subscribed capital (ASC) regime permitting returns of capital to non-resident shareholders on a tax-free basis. No zone-based profit exemption, offshore tax-holiday, or 'tax exempt zone' concession is recognised in New Zealand domestic law for stevedoring activity physically carried out within New Zealand territorial waters or port facilities.
